title: Michigan Community Revitalization Program (MCRP)
overview: The focus of the Michigan Community Revitalization Program (MCRP) is to encourage and promote the rehabilitation and redevelopment of brownfield and historic preservation sites located in traditional downtowns and high-impact corridors. It provides gap financing for innovative and/or impactful placemaking, historical redevelopment, and/or job growth.Applicants seeking $15,001 or more are subject to civil and criminal background checks. Emerging developers are encouraged.Projects must be located on eligible property, which includes facilities (contaminated), historic resources, blighted properties, functionally obsolete properties, adjacent/contiguous properties, or any other property promoting community development. Projects must demonstrate financial need, local financial support, and incorporate basic tenets of urban design.The application process involves 11 steps starting with local community review, pre-application, needs analysis, Letter of Interest (LOI), final application, statutory/financial review, MSF Board approval, legal agreements, milestone completion, and reporting.
